raw_response:
I have been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life, since I was a boy helping my father. Wheat and corn — that is what I grow. That is what my father grew, what my neighbors grow, what this land is for. I have maybe 8 mu of good flat land. In the fall I put in wheat, in the summer I follow with corn. Same land, same rotation, every year. I do not gamble on new things.

For wheat, I will go to the seed shop in town and buy the improved seed they sell — the same kind I used last year, Jimai something. It gave decent grain. I will spread the compound fertilizer and a bag of urea before planting, then another urea top-dress when the wheat is about knee-high in spring. I will water three times: once when I sow, once in spring when it starts growing fast, once when it heads. If I skip one of those, yield drops badly — I have seen it.

For corn in summer, I buy hybrid seed — everyone does, you cannot get the old varieties anymore and the hybrid really does yield more. I will apply fertilizer at planting and again when it is waist-high. Corn here does not need as much water, but if August is dry I will run the pump once.

I do not do deep plowing — that costs diesel money. I use the rotary tiller after corn harvest before wheat planting. For corn, I just drill it straight into the stubble field.

I spray once or twice each crop — herbicide early, and something for disease or insects if I see a problem. I watch the field and the neighbors' fields.
